standard.title: Manipulate elements and devices
standard.description: manipulate the elements of dance and/or choreographic devices to choreograph dances that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use elements of dance to choreograph dance that communicates ideas, perspectives and/or meaning (Y3-4). They can structure dances with beginning-middle-end, generate and combine movement material, and use choreographic intent to guide decisions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students manipulate the elements of dance and/or choreographic devices to choreograph dances that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning.

nodes.label: Choreographic devices as tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and intentionally use choreographic devices — such as repetition, contrast, unison — to shape how their dance communicates.
nodes.minimum_width: Using at least one choreographic device (e.g. repetition or contrast) intentionally in a movement sequence — can name the device and explain its effect.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring and applying choreographic devices: repetition, contrast, unison; using a repeating section that alternates with contrasting sections; structuring a dance using devices to create sections; exploring how devices change the audience experience.
wider: Investigate how choreographic devices are used in a dance they are studying or have experienced — applying the same device in their own work
Experiment with combining multiple devices in a single dance — examining how layered device use deepens communicative effect
nodes.hinge_reason: Choreographic devices are the compositional vocabulary of Y7-8 and Y9-10 Creating strand work. Students who have not internalised devices as intentional tools will approach composition as movement arrangement rather than structural craft.

response_modes.reason: Devices need naming and analysis before they become tools. Use examples from dances students have experienced — 'this section repeats, and here's what that does' — before expecting intentional application.

success_criteria: Student can name at least one choreographic device used in their dance
Student can explain what effect that device creates in their dance

nodes.label: Generating material through manipulation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can manipulate elements of dance and choreographic devices to generate and develop movement material — exploring multiple possibilities before selecting.
nodes.minimum_width: Generating at least three movement variations from one starting movement using element manipulation (space, time, dynamics, relationship); selecting among them for a choreographic purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring stimuli and other dances to devise movement possibilities (different ways to jump/land, roll/stand, spiral to ground); selecting, combining, arranging and refining; experimenting with characters and mood through element manipulation; exploring technical-expressive focus (control, coordination, balance).
wider: Use positive and negative space as a choreographic consideration — exploring how spatial relationships between dancers change meaning
Develop movement material from a theme or issue (sustainability, identity) — using element manipulation to represent ideas abstractly

response_modes.reason: Students at this level should be developing choreographic range — the habit of generating many possibilities before committing. Reward exploration over early closure.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who practise manipulating elements across diverse stimuli and themes develop genuine compositional fluency — the ability to generate purposeful material for any communicative context.
success_criteria: Student generates at least three distinct movement possibilities from one starting point
Student can explain why they selected the movements they used (connects to communicative intent)

nodes.label: Structuring a complete dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can structure a dance using choreographic devices that communicate a clear idea, perspective or meaning — with technical and expressive skill considerations integrated.
nodes.minimum_width: A structured dance using at least one device; clear communicative intent; attention to at least one technical-expressive skill (control, coordination, balance).
nodes.typical_width: Creating structured dances: narrative dances retelling a story, dances exploring themes or issues; using choreographic devices to create sections; focusing on technical and expressive skills; reflecting on and refining using Viewpoints questions ('How is the body used to represent the story?', 'How can space communicate meaning?').
wider: Create a dance using production elements (music, costume, props) to enhance communication of the theme or idea
Choreograph a dance that explores a sustainability or social issue — using device choices to structure an argument or narrative arc
nodes.hinge_reason: Producing a complete structured dance using devices — not just movement arranged in order — is the capability milestone of this standard. Without this, students enter Y7-8 without the compositional experience to work with more complex structural forms (binary, ternary, narrative) and genre-specific techniques.

response_modes.reason: Structuring integrates device knowledge (N1), generated material (N2), and technical-expressive attention into a communicative whole. Use Viewpoints questions throughout the process — not just at the end.

success_criteria: Student produces a dance that uses at least one choreographic device to structure communication of an idea
Student can identify how technical-expressive skill choices contribute to the dance's communicative effect
Student can describe what their dance communicates and explain at least one structural decision
